items.context: Round 1 decided on a costPerTurnEstimate setting (d2→A). This adds a 6th new setting. Need to nail down the range and default. Claude Code Opus costs roughly $0.03-0.15 per turn depending on context length and tool use. Sonnet is ~3-5x cheaper. The setting should be model-agnostic — users set their observed average.

options.label: Range 0.00-5.00 $/turn, default 0.10
options.rationale: Covers cheap (Haiku ~$0.01) to expensive (Opus with large context ~$0.15+) with headroom. Default of $0.10 is a reasonable mid-range for Opus. At default, a 60-turn run estimates $6.00. Recommended because it balances precision with a wide enough range to not need frequent adjustment.

options.label: Range 0.00-1.00 $/turn, default 0.05
options.rationale: Tighter range assumes most users are on cheaper models. Default of $0.05 is conservative. But could clip users on Opus with heavy context.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own range and default

items.topic: UI placement for concurrency status indicator
items.context: The spec calls for '2/3 agents running' in the graph workspace header. The HUD bar right section currently has: Settings gear, Help button, and AgentsDropdown (which already shows running activities). Two natural integration points: enhance AgentsDropdown to show the count in its trigger button, or add a separate badge in the HUD bar.

options.label: Enhance AgentsDropdown trigger to show 'N/M' count badge
options.rationale: The AgentsDropdown already owns the concept of 'running agents.' Adding a count badge (e.g., '2/3' with a colored dot) to its trigger button is natural — users click to see details. No new UI elements, just enrichment of an existing one. Recommended because it consolidates agent status into one place.

options.label: Separate status badge in HUD bar, left of AgentsDropdown
options.rationale: Always visible without hovering. Clear at a glance. But adds visual clutter to the already-compact HUD bar and creates two separate UI elements about 'running agents.'

options.label: Status in sidebar header instead of HUD bar
options.rationale: More space available. But sidebar can be collapsed, making the status invisible. Also doesn't match the spec's 'graph workspace header' location.

items.context: Circuit-broken items need a way to be manually reset before cooldown expires. The plan mentions 'reset on manual retry' but doesn't specify how. Options range from implicit (any manual queue clears it) to explicit (dedicated CLI/API command).

options.label: Implicit reset: any manual queue or retry of a circuit-broken item clears the breaker
options.rationale: Zero new API surface. If a user explicitly queues a broken item, they're saying 'try again.' The force flag already exists on queue for other blockers. Recommended because it keeps the UX simple — users don't need to learn a new command, they just re-queue.

options.label: Explicit reset: dedicated 'swarm-manager execution circuit-breaker reset <kind/name>' CLI command and API endpoint
options.rationale: Clearer intent. Separates 'reset the breaker' from 'queue for execution.' Useful if you want to inspect breaker state without retrying. But adds API surface for a relatively rare operation.

options.label: Both: implicit on queue + explicit reset command
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility. But two ways to do the same thing can confuse users and complicate documentation.

items.topic: Pending item drain strategy in the poller
items.context: Round 1 decided (d3→A) that yolo-at-capacity items stay pending and the poller picks them up. ProcessScheduledStarts() currently only handles StatusScheduled records. It needs to also drain StatusPending items when concurrency slots open. Question is how to structure this expansion.

options.label: Extend ProcessScheduledStarts() with a second pass for pending items
options.rationale: Minimal change: after the scheduled-start loop, add a second loop over pending records sorted by CreatedAt. Check concurrency limit before each start. Rename method to ProcessPendingStarts() to reflect broader scope. Recommended for simplicity — one method, one ticker, clear ordering (scheduled first, then pending).

options.label: Separate method ProcessPendingQueue() on its own ticker
options.rationale: Clean separation. Could use different tick intervals (e.g., 5s for queue drain vs 2s for scheduled). But adds another goroutine and two places to understand the start flow.

options.label: Event-driven: trigger pending drain on execution completion rather than polling
options.rationale: Most responsive — slot opens, next item starts immediately. But requires wiring completion events to the drain function, changing the current fire-and-forget completion pattern.

items.text: The execution Record struct has 25 fields and no circuit breaker state. The dedicated state file (d1→A from round 1) is confirmed as the cleanest approach — embedding in records would require cross-record aggregation on every check. The state file schema should be: {"items": {"kind/name": {"consecutive_failures": N, "last_failure": "RFC3339", "broken_at": "RFC3339|null"}}}.

plan_updates: Updated plan to reflect all round 1 decisions: d4→A changes active counting to starting+running only (was starting+running+validating+needs_review); d2→A adds costPerTurnEstimate as 6th setting with proto field 30; updated Phase 5 cost estimation to reference costPerTurnEstimate; added circuit breaker JSON schema detail.
